overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 12
overview.text: This lesson is designed to make sense of the definition of the graph of the equation y=f(x), which is quite different from the definition of the graph of f covered in the previous lesson. The ultimate goal is to show that the graph of f and the graph of y=f(x) both define the same set in the Cartesian plane. The argument that shows that these two sets are the same uses an idea that is very similar to the vertical line test. In the last lesson, the graph of f was created by a generative process (using a for-next loop). In this lesson, students see that the graph of y=f(x) is created by an if-then testing process. Note about lesson pace: Just like the last lesson, use the fact that the examples are very similar to reduce the amount of writing on the board. If a computer projection is used, point out the similarities to students.
outcomes: Students understand the meaning of the graph of y=f(x), namely ((x,y) ) x∈D and y=f(x)}.
Students understand the definitions of when a function is increasing or decreasing.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.
